reason: Retains an actual constrained-logistic-MLE counterexample to equation (36), with spatial, overlap, interior, homophily and positive-order variance guards. The three weighted-square equalities are arithmetic on entered arrays, without identifying those arrays as estimator coefficients or the values as design variances. The W1 numerical certificates, W2-W3 identifications, W5 moments/tail constant and the other W6 limit and coverage conclusions are absent. The cyclic population is extended from N=3K to all N; the subsequence still supplies the counterexample.

The asymptotic and finite conjuncts express clauses (a)-(e), with corrected score fits, the intended O_j homophily product, the corrected variance floor, and both plug-in interval conclusions. Positive finite spatial masses and integrability ensure legitimate averages; the finite nonsingularity and self-inclusive symmetric neighborhoods express the prerequisites of the displayed identities. The eventual Gram/locality formulation follows the standing all-large-sample-size convention. The supporting finite_lemmas list is not an additional list of claimed conclusions.

Retains the existence of an actual constrained MLE satisfying the guards, eventual positivity of the actual fitted-IPW variance, and convergence in probability of printedSAH divided by that actual variance to 8/25. Omits W1-W3 finite identities/comparisons and the remaining W4 expansions, individual limits, Gaussian law and coverage formula. The d=0 circle table and Bernoulli law agree with the witness, but the spatial field is realized by counting measure on singleton nodes, rather than the canonical unit-disk outcome field, and is extended to all N.

Retains both identities in (a) and the symmetric-neighborhood covariance bound and expectation identity in (b), for arbitrary fixed fits. It omits all of (c), including the actual N=32 quantities and both scaled-variance limits. Both nonempty-arm and positive-propensity hypotheses in (a) protect the displayed divisions; self-inclusion in (b) is part of the standing definition of the neighborhoods.

Retains Case B in its binary Euclidean-area realization, with all-assignment table equality, disjoint bin union, positive bin areas, negative sum and positive whole-region effect. Omits Cases A and C, the below-every-bin comparison, and grid refinement. Its positive whole-region AME refutes the reading of the unweighted negative sum as that whole-region effect; it is not a claim about the empirical application.

Retains the genuine integral aggregation, marginalized means/effects, average over nodes, nodewise range and equal-mass formulas, and positive-scale comparison/p-value invariance. It does not assert the existence of sums outside the bin range or non-identifiability from bin AMEs with varying node masses. The published empirical numbers and qualitative interpretation are not certified.

Retains the full finite twenty-node adjusted ordering reversal and a spatially admissible repeated-star witness with homophily and nondegeneracy guards. The asymptotic conclusion is only an eventual upper bound C+epsilon, with C=2 Phi(q(.975)sqrt(15/16))-1<.95, on a conjunction that excludes empty-arm and nonpositive-adjustment draws. It does not assert exact limiting coverage, validity probability tending to one, the W1-W2 spectral/moment certificates, or the remaining W3 variance/degree-of-freedom/Gaussian limits. This guarded probability is not conditional coverage.

Retains the finite cap ordering and interval inclusion, and conservative asymptotic coverage for supplied critical values at least the normal quantile, with a supplied orthonormal spectral representation. Omits the comparison between Student and normal quantiles and its universal Student-degree-of-freedom corollary. The asymptotic event is an implication from both arms being nonempty, and therefore includes empty-arm draws; this is weaker than the unguarded coverage event and is not conditional coverage.

Retains the actual boundary-constrained MLE, its maximizer conditions, the uniform 3/32 remainder-tail bound and explicit failure of the printed score expansion. The iid fair assignment law is built into prob, and overlap follows immediately. Omits the separately stated numerical/derivative/uniqueness/information and moment certificates, the sharper N-dependent bound, and the limit law. It does not refute consistency or the root-N rate.

Contains exactly the consistency and root-N conclusions under compact membership, and the O_p(N^-1) and o_p(N^-1/2) score remainders conditional on interior truth. Fixed finite-dimensional sup norm is equivalent to the Euclidean norm for all these orders. LogisticConditions explicitly supplies likelihood maximization, compactness, uniform row bounds and an eventual positive Gram lower bound; the finite product weights give independent logistic Bernoulli sampling.

Contains corrected HT unbiasedness, the expectation of the literally printed control weight, the exact equality criterion, and the constant-one, p=1/4 example. Finite arbitrary real tables are the correct abstraction of fixed potential circle averages. N>0 and propensities in (0,1) are the meaningful finite prerequisites, without an assumption of unbiasedness in the hypotheses.

Retains the concrete eight-node sharp-null Witness A and its positive-probability 101-draw array, and Witness B with its exact absolute-statistic rejection sum greater than 1/20. Using ht inside mcExceedances gives the same count as using nonnegative absolute HT, because mcExceedances itself takes absolute values. Omits the universal negative-observation assertion, signed-rule size s/2, decimal approximations, and all of the seventeen-node P=10000 Witness C. The retained finite witness does not establish failure for all large P on one fixed design.

Expresses all of (a)-(c), including arbitrary nonnegative normalized finite assignment laws, independent observed/resampled assignments via product weights, ties through non-strict exceedances, the raw rejection bound, and the exact plus-one difference. Under the sharp null the outcome-dependent statistic is a fixed function of assignment, which is exactly the quantified T. The independent finite numeric inequality exhibits that the bound can exceed alpha.

Retains only the two-node, three-atom Witness 2: well-defined bounded spatial outcomes, both zero singleton-radius AMEs, positive disk/donut AMEs, and impossibility of any real weighted combination of the supported circle AMEs equaling the donut effect. Omits Witnesses 1 and 3 and the separate node-effect and shell-mass-vector equalities. This retained witness directly refutes a common weighting of the circle AMEs.

Retains the general normalized integral of the marginalized point effect, a generic finite positive-shell decomposition and its node-average/common-positive-weight consequences, and the exact normalized annular radial measure. The finite partition identity specializes to finite spatial point masses and supported distance labels. Omits the general only-if assertion about equality with a common uniform shell-mass measure, repeated non-identifiability, and a separate comparison to uniform radial measure. The common-weight clause requires all enumerated labels to have positive weights, so it does not use zero-shell means.
